name: Back and trunk stretch
pattern: Static hold: the spine rounds, arches, twists or bends sideways to ease the back and the sides of the trunk.
setup: Start on hands and knees: hands under shoulders, knees under hips.

steps.text: Breathe out and round the whole back up toward the ceiling, chin toward the chest.
Hold gently 5-30 s, then ease back to neutral. In flows like cat-cow, move slowly through 5-6 cycles.
Come out slowly, then switch sides.

cues.cue: Move gently, in the middle of the range for the low back.
cues.why: For the low back, easy cat-camel cycles (about 6) are used to reduce spine stress rather than force end range.

cues.cue: In twists, turn from the upper back; keep the hips still and square.
cues.why: The low back has little rotation; forcing it there strains it.

cues.cue: Grow tall before you bend or twist.
cues.why: A long spine spreads the movement over many joints.

cues.cue: Ease in to a mild pull, never pain.
cues.why: Gentle stretches still gain range; stretching into pain did not help and can irritate the muscle.

cues.cue: Hold 15-30 s, 2-4 times, about 60 s in total per side.
cues.why: 30 s holds gave the same gains as 60 s; aim for at least 5 min per muscle each week, most days.

breathing: Breathe slowly and normally. Ease a little deeper as you breathe out.

tempo.note: Ease in for about 3 s, hold 15-30 s, ease out. Repeat 2-4 times each side.

mistakes.name: Forcing the twist
mistakes.looks: You yank yourself round with the arms, hips swinging with you.
mistakes.fix: Hips still, twist with your breath, go less far.
mistakes.why: Rotation piles into the low back.

mistakes.name: Sinking or crunching the low back
mistakes.looks: In back bends the low back hinges sharply while the upper back stays flat.
mistakes.fix: Lift the chest up and forward; keep glutes relaxed, go lower.
mistakes.why: One spot in the low back takes all the bend.

mistakes.name: Bouncing
mistakes.looks: You bob in and out of the stretch instead of holding still.
mistakes.fix: Ease in slowly, then stay still and let it relax.
mistakes.why: Bouncing triggers the muscle to tighten back and can strain it.

mistakes.name: Holding your breath
mistakes.looks: You tense up: shoulders creep up, jaw tight, breath held.
mistakes.fix: Breathe slowly; let each breath out take you a little deeper.
mistakes.why: Tension fights the stretch; relaxed breathing lets the muscle let go.

safety: Back pain that shoots down a leg: skip deep rounding and twisting; see a clinician.
Early in the morning the spine is stiffer: go easy on deep rounding right after waking.
Osteoporosis: avoid loaded rounding and forced twists.

variants.change: On a chair: same move with the hips on the seat, feet flat; easier to keep the pelvis still.
Over a ball: face up arches the back, face down rounds it. Keep the feet wide for balance.
Contract-relax: push gently against the stretch for 3-6 s, relax, then ease deeper. Similar range gains to static holds; also best after training.
A partner moves the limb. Go slowly and say when you feel a mild pull; the partner holds there, never pushes into pain.
Moving version: controlled swings through the range, 8-12 reps. Better before training than long holds.

subtypes.name: Cat stretch (round)
subtypes.change: On hands and knees, round the whole back up, head down.

subtypes.name: Cow stretch (arch)
subtypes.change: On hands and knees, let the belly drop and lift the chest and gaze.

subtypes.name: Side bend stretch
subtypes.change: Standing or seated tall, one arm overhead; bend sideways over the other hip, no leaning forward.

keyframes.note: trunk side-bent 25° to the right (no joint key yet; proposed trunkRot/trunkSide)

subtypes.name: Seated twist
subtypes.change: Sit tall, turn the chest toward one side, hand behind you; hips stay square.

keyframes.note: trunk twisted 40° (chest turns right) (no joint key yet; proposed trunkRot/trunkSide)

subtypes.name: Stability ball back stretch
subtypes.change: Lie back over a ball, feet wide, arms overhead, and let the spine curve over it.

subtypes.name: Lying twist
subtypes.change: On your back, knees bent, arms out; let the knees fall to one side, shoulders down.

keyframes.note: trunk twisted 40° (chest turns right) (no joint key yet; proposed trunkRot/trunkSide)

subtypes.name: Back extension stretch
subtypes.match: prone|cobra|abdominal|stomach|lean back|backbend|backward|thoracic bridge|lumbar\) extension|lower trunk flexor|t spine press
subtypes.change: Face down, hands under the shoulders; press the chest up, hips down (or lean back standing, hands on hips).

subtypes.name: Kneeling thoracic rotation
subtypes.change: On hands and knees, hand behind the head or reaching under; turn the chest up to the ceiling.

keyframes.note: trunk twisted 45° (chest turns right) (no joint key yet; proposed trunkRot/trunkSide)

subtypes.name: Standing twist
subtypes.change: Stand tall, feet planted; turn the chest to one side, hips facing forward.

keyframes.note: trunk twisted 40° (chest turns right) (no joint key yet; proposed trunkRot/trunkSide)

subtypes.name: Seated forward bend
subtypes.match: bent over back|seated lower|sitting lower trunk|cross legged|spine stretch|standing back stretch
subtypes.change: Sit with the feet flat, then fold forward and let the back round, arms hanging.

subtypes.name: Upper back stretch
subtypes.change: Hold a post or clasp your hands in front, push the arms forward and round the upper back.

subtypes.name: Knees to chest
subtypes.change: On your back, hug both knees toward the chest; let the low back round onto the floor.

metrics.label: Movement during hold
metrics.good: < 3° once you are in the stretch

motion.basis: Cat-camel cycles from mcgill2001; dose from garber2011, bandy1994, thomas2018. Twist and side bend have no joint key yet: keyframes carry them in note; mistakes and metrics use proposed keys trunkRot (+ = chest turns right) and trunkSide (+ = bend right). All angles are estimates.
